speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I am Dr. Agent, and I will be examining the skin condition on your left dorsal hand. To begin, how long have you noticed this area, and what specific symptoms like pain, itching, or swelling are you experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background. Given your history of sunbathing and diabetes, I want to focus on the specific lesion on your left dorsal hand. Is it a new growth or a change in an existing mole, and does it have any irregular borders or color variations?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis.

The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a sun-exposed area in an older adult with diabetes is highly characteristic of Actinic Keratosis. The lack of pain or tenderness is consistent with this pre-malignant lesion.
